research.topic: OBS Studio capture methods on Windows (Game/Window/Display capture, App Audio Capture, Replay Buffer), checked against the obs-studio source at master commit c5bcbca63fc32f8341c08e1f921b2b81ec46be00 (2026-10-05)
research.summary:
I read the OBS source from a sparse clone at master c5bcbca (2026-10-05) and extended the git history back to 2019 so I could read the commit messages. OBS has three video capture paths on Windows, and none of its game-oriented paths is plain screen recording.

(1) Game Capture is OBS's most efficient path. The KB says "the most efficient way… should always be tried first". It works by injecting graphics-hook64.dll into the game. By default the anti-cheat compatibility hook is ON, so inject-helper uses SetWindowsHookEx(WH_GETMESSAGE). With it off and a matching architecture, OBS injects directly: OpenProcess(PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS) + VirtualAllocEx/WriteProcessMemory/CreateRemoteThread(LoadLibraryW), with the API names obfuscated. The DLL Detours-hooks Present, ResizeBuffers and Present1 (DXGI), D3D9 Present/Reset, D3D8, D3D12 ExecuteCommandLists, and SwapBuffers/wglSwapBuffers (OpenGL). Vulkan is not hooked this way: OBS registers an implicit Vulkan layer (VK_LAYER_OBS_HOOK) under HKLM, or HKCU when not elevated. On every Present the game's own GPU copies the backbuffer into a D3D11_RESOURCE_MISC_SHARED texture, which OBS opens by shared handle. That is the GPU shared-texture path. "SLI/Crossfire Capture Mode (Slow)" (and an automatic fallback) forces the shared-memory path instead: a staging texture, Map, and memcpy in a copy thread.

Anti-cheat tolerance of this hook depends on OBS's signing certificate. Per the OBS KB, vendors exempt the certificate itself, and the 31.0 certificate change broke Vanguard and FACEIT until 31.1. A new, unknown app that injects the same way would not have that exemption.

(2) Window Capture has two methods: BitBlt (labelled "Legacy (BitBlt)") and WGC (labelled "Modern (WGC)"). Automatic mode picks BitBlt unless the window class contains "Chrome" or "Mozilla", or exactly matches a list. The list covers UWP/WinUI, Office, SDL_app, WINDOWSCLIENT (Roblox), WindowsWebview2Wrapper and the Gaming Services UI. jp9000's 2020 commit explains why BitBlt is preferred: the yellow border, no cursor control, and the forced switch away from the hardware cursor. Those problems are now handled with IsBorderRequired(false) and IsCursorCaptureEnabled. OBS's WGC code uses a 2-buffer Direct3D11CaptureFramePool with callbacks on the graphics thread, plus one extra CopyResource per frame. The source comment says: "if they gave an SRV, we could avoid this copy".

(3) Display Capture defaults to DXGI Desktop Duplication: a non-blocking AcquireNextFrame(0) followed by CopyResource. Automatic switches to WGC when DXGI cannot see the monitor (it is attached to another GPU), or when the PC has a battery and 2 or more adapters (the hybrid-laptop case).

(4) Game Capture has no WGC fallback; game-capture.c contains no WGC code. "Capture any fullscreen application" just hooks the foreground window if it covers the monitor within ±2 px. For games where hooking is blocked or needs admin (Destiny 2, Roblox, CoD and others), OBS's compatibility.json tells users to use Window Capture or Display Capture instead.

(5) Application Audio Capture uses AUDIOCLIENT_ACTIVATION_TYPE_PROCESS_LOOPBACK with PROCESS_LOOPBACK_MODE_INCLUDE_TARGET_PROCESS_TREE. It finds the PID from the window, and is only registered on build 19041 or later; the code comment says "MS says 20348". Its timestamps are WASAPI QPC positions × 100.

(6) The Replay Buffer is an in-RAM deque of refcounted encoded packets. Defaults are 15 s / 500 MB, and the MB limit is set to 0 for bitrate-based rate control. It purges a whole GOP at a time and always keeps at least 2 keyframes. Pressing save records save_ts = QPC now. The actual save happens when the next packet arrives with sys_dts_usec ≥ save_ts. The whole deque, which starts at a keyframe, is then muxed by a separate obs-ffmpeg-mux.exe process through a pipe. OBS has no native post-roll; the workarounds are delayed-save scripts, Advanced Scene Switcher or AutoHotkey.

All OBS timing runs on QPC: os_gettime_ns, the fixed-rate render grid, encoder sys_dts and WASAPI timestamps. This supports the user's idea of one in-app clock based on QPC with a measured offset between PCs, rather than each PC's wall clock.

(7) I found no official OBS benchmark comparing the cost of WGC, DXGI and hooking. The only official efficiency statements are the KB lines (game capture is most efficient; memory capture is less efficient), a source-code comment on limiting the capture framerate, and forum or volunteer advice to disable HAGS.

findings.claim: OBS's Game Capture puts its own DLL into the game. The default 'Use anti-cheat compatibility hook' (ON) launches inject-helper, which loads the DLL through SetWindowsHookEx(WH_GETMESSAGE) on the game's window thread. When the option is off and OBS and the game have the same bitness, OBS injects directly: OpenProcess(PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS), then VirtualAllocEx + WriteProcessMemory + CreateRemoteThread(LoadLibraryW). These Win32 function names are looked up through obfuscated strings. UWP apps never use the anti-cheat path.

findings.claim: Vulkan capture works differently: OBS registers graphics-hook64.dll as an implicit Vulkan loader layer, so the Vulkan loader itself loads it into every Vulkan app. The layer is written under HKLM when OBS is elevated, otherwise under HKCU. findings.claim: Game Capture has two transfer paths. Shared texture (GPU): inside the game process, the hook CopyResource's (or ResolveSubresource's) the backbuffer into a D3D11_RESOURCE_MISC_SHARED texture on each captured Present, and OBS opens that texture with gs_texture_open_shared, so nothing touches the CPU. Shared memory (CPU): used when 'SLI/Crossfire Capture Mode (Slow)' is on, or automatically when shared textures are unavailable; it copies into 3 staging textures, Maps them and memcpy's into a file mapping in a copy thread. OBS does not detect a GPU mismatch automatically; the game must run on OBS's GPU.

findings.claim: Official OBS efficiency statements: the KB calls Game Capture the most efficient method and memory capture (the SLI mode) less efficient. A source-code comment says capture must always be framerate-limited, because hooking a very high-FPS game without a limit hurts performance badly.

If a game running at 900 FPS is being captured without some sort of limited capture interval, it will dramatically reduce performance. */ if (!gc->config.limit_framerate) interval /= 2;' This means the hook copies at most 2x OBS FPS by default.

findings.claim: Anti-cheat tolerance of OBS's hook depends on OBS's code-signing certificate. The KB says switching the hook's certificate 'may require updates to anti-cheat solutions that specifically exempt the current certificate'. OBS 31.0 (ECC-only signature) broke Game Capture with Riot Vanguard, and FACEIT failed on 31.0 too; the 31.1+ dual-signed hook (new RSA + ECC) restored both, per the KB table. Valve titles need -allow_third_party_software. The OBS compatibility list also says several games 'may require OBS to be run as admin' and that others 'cannot be captured using Game Capture. Use Window Capture or Display Capture instead.'

findings.claim: What this means for a new, unknown app that copied OBS's hook approach: anti-cheats that allow OBS do so through OBS's signing certificate, so the new app's hook would have no exemption and would probably be blocked or flagged. It would also need PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS or SetWindowsHookEx into the game, and admin for elevated games. That conflicts with DuoClip's 'no injection, anti-cheat friendly, no admin' requirements.
findings.evidence: This combines three sources above: the certificate-based exemption language in the KB, the OpenProcess(PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS)/CreateRemoteThread/SetWindowsHookEx code, and the compatibility.json 'may require OBS to be run as admin' entries. No anti-cheat vendor statement about unknown hooks was found.

findings.claim: OBS developers' stated reasons for defaulting to BitBlt: WGC's yellow border, no cursor control, and WGC switching the system away from the hardware cursor. An earlier commit adds that WGC applies DPI scaling, which can blur the image. Current OBS code removes the border and controls the cursor where Windows supports it.

This was implemented because the new capture method has a number of undesired effects associated with it -- the issue of the capture border that we can do nothing about, the fact that we can't control the capture of the cursor, and the fact that Microsoft designed it to switch the cursor away from hardware cursor mode when the capture is active...'. findings.claim: How OBS implements WGC: a Direct3D11CaptureFramePool created with Create (not CreateFreeThreaded), 2 buffers, at the window's current size. FrameArrived events come through a DispatcherQueue on OBS's graphics thread, which pumps Windows messages. Each frame is copied with CopyResource (or CopySubresourceRegion for client-area capture) into an OBS-owned texture, an extra full-frame GPU copy that OBS notes it would avoid if WGC exposed an SRV. If the frame format does not match, the capture deactivates. OBS does not set MinUpdateInterval, so the frame rate follows the window's present/compose rate.

findings.claim: Every OBS timestamp is on one clock, QueryPerformanceCounter (QPC). os_gettime_ns() is QPC. The render loop timestamps frames on a fixed QPC grid; game and WGC capture just provide the newest texture at each tick, and the game's Present time is not used. Encoder packets carry system-time DTS (encoder start_ts plus relative DTS). Process-loopback audio uses the WASAPI QPC position × 100 as its timestamp. Taken together, this supports the user's proposal: one in-app clock based on QPC, with a measured offset between PCs, instead of each PC's wall clock.

findings.claim: The OBS Replay Buffer keeps encoded packets, video and audio interleaved, in an in-memory deque of reference-counted encoder_packet structures. Nothing goes to disk until a save. Limits are max_time_sec (default 15) and max_size_mb (default 500). The UI sets max_size_mb to 0, meaning no size limit, when a bitrate-based rate control is used. Old data is purged one GOP at a time: the front keyframe and everything up to the next video keyframe. Purging stops while 2 or fewer keyframes remain, so the buffer always starts on a keyframe and its length is between about max_time minus one GOP and max_time.

findings.claim: How a replay save works: the hotkey or proc 'save()' only records save_ts = os_gettime_ns()/1000, which is QPC. On the encoder output thread, the first packet whose sys_dts_usec ≥ save_ts triggers replay_buffer_save(). That function copies the whole deque into a new array, re-bases video and per-track audio timestamps to the first packet, and pipes everything to a separate obs-ffmpeg-mux.exe process on a mux thread. So the clip ends at the hotkey moment, with encoder latency accounted for. It does not cut at an exact time: the clip starts at the oldest kept keyframe. There is no native post-roll; the only options are 'void save()' and 'get_last_replay'.
findings.evidence: obs-ffmpeg-mux.c:917-932 save_replay_proc: `stream->save_ts = os_gettime_ns() / 1000LL;`. :1227-1237 `if (stream->save_ts && packet->sys_dts_usec >= stream->save_ts) { if (os_atomic_load_bool(&stream->muxing)) return; ... stream->save_ts = 0; replay_buffer_save(stream); }`. replay_buffer_save:1125-1178: offsets from the first video pts and the first audio dts per track, insert_packet() rebases them, then `pthread_create(&stream->mux_thread, NULL, replay_buffer_mux_thread, stream)`. :114 `#define FFMPEG_MUX "obs-ffmpeg-mux.exe"`; :310 `os_process_pipe_create2(args, "w")`. :948-949 only `"void save()"` and `"void get_last_replay(out string path)"` are registered. frontend/widgets/OBSBasic_ReplayBuffer.cpp:154-168 ReplayBufferSave() just calls proc 'save'.

findings.claim: Post-roll in the OBS ecosystem is done only by workarounds. Users set a longer buffer and delay the save call with a script timer, Advanced Scene Switcher or AutoHotkey. Plugins and scripts such as 'Additional Replay Buffer' and Replay Buffer Pro trim the saved file afterwards (backward from the save point). Exeldro's Replay Source keeps N seconds of a source in memory for instant replay and has save-to-disk but no post-roll. No plugin was found that adds true native post-roll.
findings.evidence: Forum 'Can replay buffer record X seconds after pushing hotkey?': answer 'Not really, no. Just set the clip-capture for 15 seconds, and wait the extra 5 seconds yourself before hitting the button'. Forum 'Replay buffer - record after hotkey': reply suggests a second, delayed hotkey press via AutoHotkey or Advanced Scene Switcher. 'Additional Replay Buffer' resource clips seconds from the beginning/end of the saved replay. Replay Buffer Pro (search extract; page not fetchable) saves and trims to custom durations, needs OBS 32.2.0+. exeldro/obs-replay-source README: 'Keeps the configured seconds from a source in memory', 'Save replay' hotkey, delay options only for playback.

findings.claim: No official OBS benchmark or developer statement ranking WGC, DXGI duplication and the hook by CPU/GPU cost was found. Forum replies treat the methods as a compatibility choice. OBS forum support replies say Windows HAGS is 'known to cause performance and capture issues with OBS, games and overlay tools' and recommend disabling it, but this is volunteer advice, not KB text.
findings.evidence: Forum 'Game capture, Window capture, or Display capture, what's the actual difference in performance?': 'While I cannot answer whether one of these capture methods have better performance, I can answer why different capture methods exist: it's for compatibility reasons.' Forum (videos-come-out-choppy thread): 'The Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling ("HAGS") feature in Windows is currently known to cause performance and capture issues with OBS, games and overlay tools. It's an experimental feature and we recommend disabling it'. Code-level fact: WGC and DXGI paths in OBS each do one full-frame CopyResource per frame (see the findings above); the hook copies inside the game process, capped at ≤2x OBS FPS.

design_recommendations: On whether screen recording is the most effective method: OBS's most efficient path (the KB calls it 'most efficient') is not screen recording but DLL injection (Game Capture shared texture). DuoClip rules out injection, and anti-cheats exempt OBS's hook by OBS's certificate, so a new hook would not be tolerated. Use Windows.Graphics.Capture (WGC) window capture as the primary method. This is the non-injection path OBS itself auto-selects for SDL_app, Roblox (WINDOWSCLIENT), UWP/WinUI and Chromium windows, and the one OBS points users to when Game Capture is blocked (Destiny 2, Roblox). Avoid full-display capture (DXGI duplication) as the default: it records everything on screen (Discord pop-ups, notifications, second app), which is worse for privacy. [inferred from the OBS code/KB findings]

WGC settings, following OBS: call GraphicsCaptureAccess::RequestAccessAsync(Borderless) and IsBorderRequired(false), and IsCursorCaptureEnabled as wanted, guarded by ApiInformation.IsPropertyPresent; require D3D11 and build 18362 or later (UniversalApiContract 8). Improve on OBS: use Direct3D11CaptureFramePool.CreateFreeThreaded on a dedicated high-priority capture thread instead of the render thread, and feed the WGC surface straight into the GPU colour-convert/scale pass and the encoder input. That removes the extra CopyResource OBS admits to ('if they gave an SRV, we could avoid this copy'). Measure GPU/FPS cost against ShadowPlay and Medal on the target games. [inferred]

Fallback ladder, modelled on OBS's auto-selection: (a) WGC window capture; (b) WGC or DXGI monitor capture cropped to the game window's rectangle, for true exclusive-fullscreen titles where window capture shows black. For (b), apply OBS's rule: use DXGI if the monitor is on the encoding GPU, and WGC if DXGI cannot enumerate it, or if there is a battery and 2 or more adapters (hybrid laptops). Tell users of hybrid laptops to run the game and DuoClip on the same discrete GPU, as OBS's KB does. [primary for OBS logic, inferred for applying it to DuoClip]

One shared clock: use QPC everywhere, as OBS does (os_gettime_ns = QPC; WASAPI process loopback timestamp = u64QPCPosition×100; encoder sys_dts = QPC-based). Never use DateTime or wall clock for sync. Exchange QPC timestamps between peers and estimate the offset/drift in the QPC domain (NTP-style over the data channel, several samples, take the minimum RTT). Timestamp each video frame with the WGC frame's SystemRelativeTime (QPC-based) instead of OBS's approach of sampling on its render grid, so each frame keeps its real capture moment. [OBS facts primary; SystemRelativeTime usage inferred, not from OBS]

Post-roll (recording a few seconds after the press): OBS has none natively, but its save mechanism generalizes easily. Instead of save_ts = now, set save_ts = press_qpc + M. Each peer converts the clipper's press time into its own QPC using the measured offset. Each peer waits until its encoder emits a packet with sys_dts ≥ press + M, then snapshots the range [press - N, press + M] from the ring. Size the ring for N + M + 1 GOP + network/offset margin, e.g. 30 + 10 + 1 + 2 s. Like OBS, never purge below 2 keyframes. [inferred from obs-ffmpeg-mux.c logic]

Buffer and temporary-clip storage ('bucket'): copy OBS's approach for the live buffer, an in-RAM ring of refcounted encoded packets purged one whole GOP at a time with both time and MB caps. Note that OBS drops the MB cap for bitrate-based rate control, but DuoClip should keep it. When a clip is saved, write the selected packet range to a local temp file (OBS muxes in a separate obs-ffmpeg-mux.exe process through a pipe, which isolates crashes). Only then upload the proxy or full-quality range to a temporary object-storage bucket with a short time-to-live, or send it P2P. OBS has no cloud or bucket feature, so this part is DuoClip's own design. [inferred]

Exact start/end: OBS clips start at the oldest keyframe in the buffer, so the start is imprecise by up to one GOP. With 1 s keyframes, choose the keyframe at or before press - N and store the exact in-point as an edit offset or edit list. Any frame-accurate trim in the editor then needs re-encoding of only the first and last GOP (smart render) or a full re-encode on export. [inferred]

Audio: use process loopback exactly as OBS does: AUDIOCLIENT_ACTIVATION_TYPE_PROCESS_LOOPBACK with INCLUDE_TARGET_PROCESS_TREE, the PID taken from the game's window and from Discord's main window, a 32-bit float format you choose, event callback, and a buffer of several seconds. Enable it on build 19041 or later like OBS, but log and test, since Microsoft documents 20348. Keep game and Discord on separate tracks with per-packet QPC timestamps (ts×100). Note that OBS Game Capture refuses discord.exe, which is irrelevant here because only Discord's audio is needed. [primary for OBS facts]

Performance hygiene borrowed from OBS: limit the capture/encode rate to a fixed output fps (OBS warns uncapped capture of a 900 fps game 'will dramatically reduce performance'). Detect and log HAGS state and multi-GPU topology at startup for support and diagnostics, since OBS support attributes many capture and performance issues to HAGS. [primary for OBS statements; inferred for DuoClip]
open_questions: No official OBS benchmark was found comparing the GPU/CPU cost of WGC window capture, DXGI duplication and the Game Capture shared-texture hook. DuoClip needs its own measurements on target games (e.g. CS2, Valorant, Fortnite, LoL) on mid-range hardware common in Brazil.

Does WGC window capture work for true exclusive-fullscreen (non-flip-model) games, or do they show black? This is not addressed in OBS code or the KB; it needs testing to decide when to fall back to monitor capture.

The current state (October 2026) of the KB 'Capture Hook Certificate Update' anti-cheat table could not be confirmed: obsproject.com and iris.obsproject.com were unreachable from this environment, and the last snapshot seen via search is dated 2025-06-03. It matters only as evidence that anti-cheats exempt OBS by certificate.
Medal's actual capture method is outside this topic and was not researched here. Whether Medal uses WGC, DXGI or a signed hook should come from a separate Medal-focused investigation.

Does Discord's voice audio play from a process inside the process tree of the window-owning Discord.exe, so that OBS-style PID-from-window plus INCLUDE_TARGET_PROCESS_TREE captures it? This needs testing on current Discord builds.
Does Windows' WGC 'MinUpdateInterval' (not used by OBS) or the frame pool's buffer count affect latency or FPS cost for high-refresh games? Not covered by OBS sources.
Is the HAGS guidance still current on Windows 11 24H2/25H2? The advice found is from OBS forum volunteers (2024), not the official KB.

research.topic: Which capture methods Medal (medal.tv Windows client) uses, and how its replay buffer, clipping, post-roll and clip storage/upload work
research.summary: Medal's Windows recorder is a hybrid. It does not rely on screen recording alone, and it is not an OBS fork. Its default path is an injected game hook, and two non-injection window-capture paths sit beside it. The hook is medal-hook32.dll / medal-hook64.dll, derived from OBS's graphics-hook. Medal 3.696 logs (Aug 2023) show "[ESM State]: OBSInjectionState", "Injecting into process", "[OBSCaptureState] Shared texture success", and a [d3d8]/[d3d9]/[dxgi] offsets block in exactly the format OBS's get-graphics-offsets.c prints. A third-party trace shows Medal creating window class "medal_temp_d3d_window_4039785" titled "Temp Window", the same magic name OBS's graphics-hook.c uses ("temp_d3d_window_4039785"). Static analysis of recorder v2638.2751.1 (Sept 2026) still finds MedalEncoder.OBS.HookInterface/BaseHookInterface/GraphicsOffsets classes, a Host folder with injection helpers and graphics hooks, and a Licenses/obs_source_offer.txt for those OBS-derived (GPLv2) parts. Medal's own antivirus article says "Medal injects into your games so that it can give you an overlay and capture your gameplay". Its 2026 marketing pages say the opposite ("does not inject into games or interact with anti-cheat systems"). The shipped binaries contradict that marketing claim. The recording methods Medal exposes map as follows. Game capture is the injected OBS-style DXGI/D3D Present hook with a shared texture, preferred by default (PreferGameCapture=true). Force Window Capture is a non-injection window capture that only works in windowed or borderless mode. In 2023 the standard window capture was DXGI-based (log "Capture mode: DXGI", "Capture area is 0,24,1920,1040", window focus/move WinEvent hooks, and an inactiveGame.png placeholder on GameWindowDefocus). That is very likely Desktop Duplication cropped to the window, which explains the "Game out of Focus" error (inferred). Advanced Window Capture is Windows.Graphics.Capture. The 2023 RPC is literally "set.windowsGraphicsCapture" -> "Saving Advanced Window Capture", and the feature shows the yellow border controlled by the Windows 11 "Graphics capture" privacy toggle. It also fails in exclusive fullscreen and hides the cursor. Experimental Capture exists as a setting key (ExperimentalCapture) but its technique was not found. Desktop/Screen capture is monitor capture; its API (DXGI duplication vs WGC) is not confirmed. The engine changed over time. It was FFmpeg CLI at first, then Medialooks MFormats SDK (vendor case study; 2023 logs show MFORMATSLib.MFLiveClass, codec 'a264hw', NV12). In 2026 it is a .NET 4.6.2 MedalEncoder.exe over a native 'scope.dll' that imports D3D11/DXGI/D3D9/D2D/DWM/AVRT plus FFmpeg. scope.dll exposes window/screen/texture capture targets, GPU/CPU encoders, process-audio targets, a WHIP output, and memory/disk/mmap replay buffers with export_from_timestamp. Medal auto-selects NVENC/AMF/Quick Sync, defaults to H.264 (HEVC optional, AV1 early access) with CPU fallback, and defaults to VFR. The buffer defaults to RAM and can be moved to disk. In 2023 a 120 s, 10 Mbps buffer was logged as 180 MB, so it holds encoded packets sized about bitrate x length x 1.2. Clip lengths run 15 s to 20 min, and the default hotkey action is "clip;length=30". The manual hotkey only looks backward. Medal does support post-roll for event-triggered clips: its Game API's captureDelayMs means "milliseconds Medal waits after the request before snapshotting the replay buffer", and portal events set "seconds before and after". That is the same delayed-export technique DuoClip needs. On the cloud side, uploaded clips are served from cdn.medal.tv/ugcc/content/<id>.mp4 with an "auth=exp=...~data=...~hmac=..." token, an Akamai EdgeAuth-style signed URL (provider inferred). A 2026 Medal job post lists GCP (GKE, Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, GCS, Pub/Sub, BigQuery) behind a Cloudflare + Akamai edge. Medal uses "Progressive Upload" (draft, then save) and 14-day expiring share links that renew on copy, which is a direct precedent for a TTL'd temporary-clip bucket. No evidence was found that Medal is whitelisted by, or partnered with, Vanguard, FACEIT, EAC, BattlEye or Ricochet. Medal's own black-clip article lists FACEIT Anti-Cheat among software that interferes with "Medal's hook", and public crash investigations blame medal-hook64.dll. Cheat projects also reuse Medal's hook. All of this supports DuoClip's no-injection, WGC-first plan, with a documented fallback for exclusive fullscreen. Access caveat: medal.tv, support.medal.tv, medium.com and blog.medialooks.com were blocked by the egress proxy (403/ENOTFOUND). Medal page text therefore comes from search-result excerpts, and the installer was not downloaded.

findings.claim: Medal exposes these recording modes and settings: Clip Mode (hotkey replay buffer), Screenshots, Long Recording / Full Session Recording, and Desktop Capture (Screen Recording). The advanced recording toggles are Force Window Capture, Advanced Window Capture, Experimental Capture and HDR Compatibility, plus an In-Memory Buffer (RAM vs Disk) choice. The 2026 recorder's setting keys include AdvancedWindowCapture, ExperimentalCapture, ForceWindowCapture, PreferGameCapture (default true), HDRCompatibility, InMemoryBuffer (default true), ScreenCaptureEnabled, FullSessionMode, FpsMode (default VFR), Codec (default H264) and Encoder (default GPU).
findings.evidence: The support article 'How To Choose Your Recording Method' lists Clip Mode (F8; 15/30/45/60/120 s, longer up to 20 min), Screenshots, Long Recording ('Full Session Recording' in an older revision) and Desktop Capture. The 'What is Advanced Window Capture?' and 'Black Clips / Stuck in 1 frame' articles name Force Window Capture, Advanced Window Capture and Experimental Capture under Settings > Advanced > Advanced | Recording. 'Bright / Overexposed Clips' names HDR Compatibility. The third-party settings_catalog.json extracted from client 2637.461.1 / recorder 2638.2751.1 lists recorderKeys including AdvancedWindowCapture, ExperimentalCapture, ForceWindowCapture, PreferGameCapture, HDRCompatibility and InMemoryBuffer, with defaults PreferGameCapture:true, InMemoryBuffer:true, FpsMode:'VFR', Codec:'H264', Encoder:'GPU'.

findings.claim: Medal's default 'game capture' injects a hook DLL (medal-hook32.dll / medal-hook64.dll) into the game process. The hook takes over DXGI/D3D Present and ResizeBuffers and hands frames back through a shared GPU texture.
findings.evidence: A public Medal 3.696 log (Aug 2023) shows: line 644 '----[ESM State]: OBSInjectionState----', line 645 'Injecting into process 3568', line 647 'Attempting to hook... [0]', line 676 '[ESM State]: GameCapture', line 689 '[OBSCaptureState] Shared texture success ... Format: R8G8B8A8_UNorm', line 726 'GameRecordingSuccessfullyStarted InjectionCapture'. Another log (line 101) shows Medal setting permissions on '...\Medal\recorder-3.696.0\Host\medal-hook64.dll'. A New World crash investigation found '<user-appdata>\Medal\HookDLL\MedalHook_<pid>\medal-hook64.dll (per-PID hook injected by Medal.tv)' loaded in the game process. Cheat/overlay repos pattern-scan medal-hook64.dll to hijack its Present/ResizeBuffers hooks.

findings.claim: Medal's game hook is derived from OBS Studio's win-capture graphics-hook (GPL-2.0). Medal ships a source offer for the OBS-derived components.
findings.evidence: (1) Medal's log at MedalLog20230804.txt ~lines 657-671 prints '[d3d8] present=... [d3d9] present= present_ex= present_swap= d3d9_clsoff= is_d3d9ex_clsoff= [dxgi] present= present1= resize= release='. That is byte-for-byte the printf format of OBS plugins/win-capture/get-graphics-offsets/get-graphics-offsets.c lines 33-45. (2) A Frida trace shows Medal creating 'class=medal_temp_d3d_window_4039785 title=Temp Window'. OBS graphics-hook.c line 193 uses L"temp_d3d_window_4039785" and line 207 uses L"Temp Window". (3) Static analysis of MedalEncoder.exe v2638.2751.1 finds the P/Invoke classes MedalEncoder.OBS.HookInterface, MedalEncoder.OBS.BaseHookInterface and MedalEncoder.OBS.GraphicsOffsets (NtOpenSection, MapViewOfFile, NtOpenEvent, NtCreateMutant: OBS game-capture IPC style). The same analysis says 'The Host directory contains injection helpers and graphics hooks. Licenses/obs_source_offer.txt specifically identifies OBS-derived components in Host'. (4) Toolscreen's bug tracker says 'Medal masquerades as OBS hook (medal-hook64.dll)'. OBS COPYING is GPL v2.

findings.claim: Medal officially acknowledges injection in its support docs, but its 2026 marketing pages claim it does not inject. The shipped recorder still contains the injection machinery.
findings.evidence: The support article 'How to whitelist Medal in your Anti-Virus' says: 'Medal injects into your games so that it can give you an overlay and capture your gameplay. Injection is a common method for recorders, mods and other programs, and this is what the anti-virus finds.' The black-clips article says 'Some overlays and recorders may interfere with Medal's hook'. Medal's learn pages (e.g. how-to-clip-on-pc) say: 'Medal does not inject into games or interact with anti-cheat systems. It will not get you banned in any game... It records your screen using hardware-accelerated encoding and runs as a separate process.' Medal's Aug 2025 job post asks the hire to 'Deeply integrate with games to detect events and gather data'.

findings.claim: 'Advanced Window Capture' is Windows.Graphics.Capture (WGC).
findings.evidence: The Medal 3.696 log maps the UI toggle to an RPC named for WGC: line 283 'Executing Request: set.windowsGraphicsCapture' followed by line 287 'Saving Advanced Window Capture 0'. Medal's article describes a yellow border that is 'a Windows security feature', removable on Windows 11 via Settings > Privacy & security > Graphics capture > 'Let apps turn off the screenshot border' (the GraphicsCaptureSession.IsBorderRequired permission). It also 'will not work if your game is in exclusive fullscreen mode'. The black-clips article warns AWC may make 'your mouse cursor invisible'. A Medal forum reply says AWC is skipped for OpenGL games such as Minecraft 'to avoid issues like the mouse cursor not being recorded'.

findings.claim: Medal's 'standard' non-injected window capture in 2023 was DXGI-based, most likely Desktop Duplication of the monitor cropped to the game window. That design explains the 'Game out of Focus' error that AWC/WGC is said to prevent.
findings.evidence: For RobloxPlayerBeta (Win32), Medal 3.696 entered '[ESM State]: WindowCaptureStandard' and logged 'Capture area is 0,24,1920,1040', 'Screen: 0', '[ESM Event] - WindowCaptureSetMonitor', 'WindowCaptureMoved' and 'Capture mode: DXGI'. It also set up WinEvent hooks for window location/focus/destroy/reorder. At capture start it created a placeholder 'Creating overlay frame from: ...\Assets\inactiveGame.png' and logged frequent '[ESM Event] - GameWindowDefocus'. Medal says AWC 'allows you to capture gameplay seamlessly, even when your game window is minimized. This feature prevents the "Game out of Focus" error'. A screen-region capture can only see what is on screen, so Medal must substitute a placeholder when the game loses focus or is covered (inference).

findings.claim: 'Force Window Capture' turns off the injected game hook and forces a window-capture path. It only works in windowed or borderless mode.
findings.evidence: The black-clips article: 'Force Window Capture: Settings > Advanced > Advanced | Recording... This works only for Windowed or Borderless games (not Exclusive Fullscreen).' For OpenGL games on Windows 11 24H2+ it recommends enabling Force Window Capture and Advanced Window Capture together. The 2026 settings contain both ForceWindowCapture (default false) and PreferGameCapture (default true), so the inference is that by default Medal prefers the hook and Force Window Capture overrides it.

findings.claim: Medal picks the capture method per game, using a local game database and per-game settings. In 2023 the same game (Roblox) was hooked in its UWP/Store build but recorded with non-injected DXGI window capture in its Win32 build.
findings.evidence: Log 'GameDB: ...\recorder-3.696.0\MedalGameInfo.db'. MedalLog20230804.txt line 630 'Game Found Type UWP (UWP): Roblox' was followed by OBSInjectionState/InjectionCapture. 'Game Found Type ProcessClass: Roblox' (RobloxPlayerBeta) was followed by WindowCaptureStandard / 'Capture mode: DXGI' in every Win32 session. OBS users report that Roblox's Byfron/Hyperion anti-tamper blocks game-capture hooks while the Microsoft Store build does not. That this is why Medal avoided injecting into the Win32 build is an inference. The 2025 changelog mentions improved capture for clients that rebuild windows, and the 2023 changelog says 'upgraded the capture method for GTA V'.

findings.claim: Which technique 'Experimental Capture' uses was not found.
findings.evidence: Medal only says: 'If Advanced Window Capture does not resolve your issues, try the Experimental Capture option available in the Advanced Recording settings.' The 2026 setting key ExperimentalCapture exists (default false). The native scope.dll exports scope_vcap_window_mode_support and scope_vcap_screen_mode_support, which implies several window and screen capture modes, but the mode names were not recovered. No Reddit, Twitter or Discord explanation was found.

findings.claim: Desktop Capture / Screen Recording records a whole monitor or a chosen window. The underlying API (DXGI Desktop Duplication vs WGC monitor capture) is not confirmed. Uploading desktop recordings requires Premium.
findings.evidence: Medal: 'On multi-monitor setups you pick which screen to record... Anyone can record their desktop, but you must have premium if you want to upload your desktop recordings.' The Windows screen-recording article offers full screen, a specific monitor or a single application window. scope.dll exposes scope_vcap_create_screen_target and imports DXGI and DWM. The 2023 recorder used a DXGI capture mode. Which API the desktop mode uses is an inference.

findings.claim: Medal's overlay has an injected DirectX mode, needed for exclusive fullscreen, alongside a normal window (Electron) overlay.
findings.evidence: Overlay FAQ options: On / 'Exclusive Fullscreen Only' ('will not work for Borderless Fullscreen games') / 'Windowed Only' / Off. The 2023 log shows 'Overlay Injected Mode setting is False', 'Electron overlay support- Enabled:False - Capture Type:DXGI' and 'Starting DirectX overlay for Roblox'. The 2026 client registers an 'overlayInjected' handler.

findings.claim: Medal's engine history: an FFmpeg-based first app, then the Medialooks MFormats SDK (used by the 2023 recorder), and in 2026 a .NET MedalEncoder over Medal's own native 'scope.dll', which uses FFmpeg.
findings.evidence: A Medialooks case study, 'Medal captures game moments with MFormats', says Medal's first desktop app drove FFmpeg and had no audio and no frame control. The team considered an FFmpeg wrapper and Media Foundation before choosing MFormats, which let them create frames manually. The study was read only via search excerpt; the page was blocked. 2023 logs show 'MFORMATSLib.MFLiveClass.PropsSet', 'codecName- a264hw, fcc type- eMFCC_NV12' and 'MedalWriter started. Bitrate: 10M'. Third-party static analysis of v2638.2751.1 found MedalEncoder.exe targeting .NET Framework 4.6.2 with SharpDX and NAudio, and ScopeSharp.dll wrapping native scope.dll, which 'imports Windows graphics/desktop libraries (D3D11/DXGI/D3D9/D2D/DWM/AVRT) and FFmpeg'. Medal's 2025 job post lists 'C#/.NET, FFmpeg, C++, and graphics APIs (DirectX, Vulkan, OpenGL)'.

findings.claim: The 2026 native engine is a source → processing → encoder → buffer/mux/output pipeline. Its replay buffers come in memory, disk and mmap types, are separate for audio and video, and can be exported from a timestamp.
findings.evidence: scope.dll imports seen through ScopeSharp P/Invoke: scope_vcap_create_window_target, scope_vcap_create_screen_target, scope_vcap_create_texture_target, scope_vcap_get_trimmed_window_rect, scope_vcap_last_frame_received_time, scope_venc_create_gpu, scope_venc_create_cpu, scope_vid_stabiliser_create, scope_vid_stabiliser_get_duplicate_frame_fps, scope_io_vid_memory_buffer_create, scope_io_vid_disk_buffer_create, scope_io_vid_mmap_buffer_create (plus aud_ variants), scope_io_buffer_exportable_start_time / exportable_end_time, scope_io_buffer_export, scope_io_buffer_export_from_timestamp, scope_io_whip_output_create, scope_frametime_now, scope_vid_frame_source_time, scope_acap_create_process_target, scope_acap_is_process_target_supported.

findings.claim: Encoders: Medal auto-selects the GPU hardware encoder (NVENC, AMF or Quick Sync), defaults to H.264, offers H.265, has AV1 in early access, and falls back to CPU encoding when the GPU has no encoder.
findings.evidence: Medal learn page: 'Medal automatically uses whichever hardware encoder is available (NVENC, AMF, or Quick Sync)'. The Video Quality Settings Guide covers H.264 (recommended), H.265 (1440p+) and AV1 ('only available on Medal's Early Access build'). The AMD GPU article says Medal 'can fall back to CPU-based recording'. 2023 log: 'Found encoder: AMD AMF HW H.264 Encoder', 'Video codec set: a264hw - hardware encoding' with NV12 input. 2026 defaults: Encoder 'GPU', Codec 'H264'. scope.dll has both venc_create_gpu and venc_create_cpu.

findings.claim: The replay buffer holds encoded packets, in RAM by default with a disk option, sized roughly as bitrate x clip length plus headroom. The 2023 RAM buffer for 120 s at 10 Mbps was 180 MB.
findings.evidence: Support article 'What is the recording buffer' (2022): the buffer can be on Hard disk or Memory (RAM); RAM applies only in Clip Mode, and Full Session reverts to Disk. 'For the highest quality options (144fps, 100M bitrate) Medal will need at least 3 GB of free memory'. RAM is offered to reduce SSD wear; if clips are corrupt, switch back to Disk. 2023 log: 'In Memory Buffer setting is True', clip length 120, bitrate 10, and 'Memory buffer size (MB): 180'. 10 Mbit/s x 120 s = 150 MB, so 180 MB is about 1.2x (inferred). Learn page: 'If you never press the button, the buffer is discarded and no storage is used.'

findings.claim: Clip lengths and modes: hotkey clips save 15/30/45/60/120 s and longer options up to 20 minutes. Different hotkeys can have different lengths. The 2026 default action is 'clip;length=30'. In Long Recording the clip hotkey becomes a Bookmark key, and clips cut from it are capped at 2 min (10 min with Premium).
findings.evidence: 'How To Choose Your Recording Method': 'save the previous 15, 30, 45, 60, and 120 seconds... longer clip times that go up to 20 minutes'. The learn page says 15 s to 10 min, which is inconsistent. Long Recording articles: Alt+F7 starts or stops it, and 'the Clip Hotkey (Default: F8) will change into a Bookmark Key'; clips 'up to 2 minutes long, or up to 10 minutes if you have Medal Premium'. Defaults from 2026 settings: Hotkeys [{action:'clip;length=30', inputs:'F8'}, {action:'segment_toggle', inputs:'ALT + F7'}, bookmark, switch_game F10, screenshot F7]. The recorder has no saveClip RPC; hotkeys are handled natively.

findings.claim: Post-roll: the manual hotkey only saves footage before the press, but Medal does support 'seconds after' for event-triggered clips by delaying the replay-buffer snapshot (captureDelayMs, and before/after per event).
findings.evidence: Medal: 'When you press your clipping hotkey, Medal saves the selected amount of gameplay immediately preceding the key press as a clip.' No hotkey post-roll option was found; feedback #4004 only asks to pick a length after clipping. Medal's Game API (POST http://localhost:12665/api/v1/event/invoke) has clipOptions.duration and captureDelayMs. The YoYoGames spec, transcribed from medal.tv/developer/auto-clipping, says: 'Milliseconds Medal waits after the request before snapshotting the replay buffer. Useful for catching a killcam'. Medal's Roblox sample uses '{ duration = 30, captureDelayMs = 5000 }', annotated as '5s after the trigger; 25s before'. Developer-portal events define 'how many seconds to keep before and after the event' (example '15 seconds before and 15 seconds after').

findings.claim: Audio: Medal captures game-only audio and per-app tracks with WASAPI process loopback and falls back to device loopback. The 2026 default audio config already splits by process into game, Medal and Discord.exe sources on separate tracks.
findings.evidence: 2023 logs: '[SDK] LoopbackCapture::ActivateAudioInterface - failed to activate process loopback audio interface: HR 8000FFFF', '[SDK] GameAudioCapture::AddStream - failed to init GAO', 'Setup Loopback Audio', and 'Audio hook was found while the loopback was still in. Stopping the loopback...'. Those failures were on Windows 10 19045; the log shows OSVersion 10.0.19045. Settings show 'Game Audio Only setting is True'. 2026 defaults: AudioModeConfig {type:'splitByProcess', sources:[game-audio, MedalEncoder.exe, Discord.exe]} and MultipleAudioTracks:true. scope.dll has acap_create_process_target and acap_is_process_target_supported. Microsoft documents process loopback as requiring Windows 10 build 20348+.

findings.claim: Anti-cheat: no evidence was found that Medal is whitelisted by, or partnered with, Vanguard, FACEIT, EAC, BattlEye or Ricochet. Medal's hook is documented as conflicting with FACEIT AC and has been blamed for game crashes.
findings.evidence: The black-clips article lists 'Faceit Anti-Cheat' with OBS, ShadowPlay, Discord, RTSS and others as software that may 'interfere with Medal's hook'. A New World crash analysis names medal-hook64.dll's swapchain hook as the leading suspect. Riot, FACEIT and Epic appear only as account-linking integrations (Riot account for Valorant/LoL auto-clips). A feedback post requesting a FACEIT collaboration is user-made. Searches for Medal anti-cheat allowlisting returned nothing. OBS's equivalent graphics-hook64.dll has been blocked by BattlEye (obs-studio issue #2581).

findings.claim: Other software treats medal-hook64.dll as a known foreign injected module, and cheat developers reuse it.
findings.evidence: SpecialK dxgi_util.cpp line 2446: '// Ignores something called "medal-hook64.dll"'. The Phostwood crash-analyzer maps 'medal-hook64.dll' to 'Medal.tv Hook Library - used for game recording'. Arcane's 2026-09-22 research lists medal-hook64.dll among injected overlay modules. wows-toolkit-hardening tests flag ...\Medal\medal-hook64.dll as foreign. AltoidUC/medal-overlay-hook is described as 'Hijack Medal.tv's in-game overlay for rendering onto the screen with DirectX11'.

findings.claim: Medal tunes the system for recording: it disables Windows Game Mode by default and raises its own GPU scheduling priority and frame latency. The 2026 recorder also checks HAGS status.
findings.evidence: 2023 log line 173 'Disabling windows game mode to improve performance..' followed by 'Windows game mode disabled.'. Elsewhere: 'IncreaseFrameLatency success', 'Failed to enable base priority privilege!', 'SetGPUPriority result: 6'. 2026 defaults include WindowsGameModeDisabled:true. Recorder P/Invoke classes include MedalEncoder.GPUSchedulingUtility+HAGSStatus+D3DKMTFunctions. The 2024 changelog notes GPU thread priority tweaks.

findings.claim: Clip hosting: uploaded clips are served from cdn.medal.tv with an expiring HMAC-signed token in Akamai EdgeAuth format. Medal's backend runs on Google Cloud (GCS and others) behind a Cloudflare + Akamai edge.
findings.evidence: 2023 log line 806: 'Content uploaded ID: ... URL: https://cdn.medal.tv/ugcc/content/<id>.mp4?auth=exp=1691166600~data=...~hmac=...'. The 'exp=~data=~hmac=' layout matches Akamai EdgeAuth tokens; identifying the provider from that format is an inference. Medal job post (Jul 2026, covering General Intuition and Medal's creator platform): 'Cloud: GCP (GKE, Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, GCS, Pub/Sub, BigQuery), Cloudflare + Akamai edge.' Medal's WARP troubleshooting lists cdn.medal.tv among domains to exclude.

findings.claim: Medal's temporary-clip model: 14-day expiring 'private links' that renew when the link is copied, a permanent 'Post to Profile', a Premium cloud sync, and auto-upload timing that defaults to after the game exits. The desktop client uses a two-step 'Progressive Upload' (draft, then save).
findings.evidence: Expiring Links article: Create Link makes a temporary link available for 14 days; Copy Link resets the countdown; after expiry the local file stays; Post to Profile keeps it indefinitely. Auto Upload FAQ: upload instantly, after the game closes (recommended), or never; Medal warns instant uploads 'may impact your bandwidth while gaming'. 2026 default AutoUploadOption:'ON_GAME_EXIT'. 2023 log: '[Progressive Upload] Content draft request ...' → 'Content draft ... reply status OK' → '[Progressive Upload] Content save ... reply status=202', and setting 'Progressive uploads setting is False'.

findings.claim: Advanced Window Capture was announced around February 2021.
findings.evidence: Medal_TV tweet ID 1357756453977784320, titled 'Advanced Window Capture Under Settings >...'. The tweet's snowflake ID decodes to 2021-02-05 18:22 UTC; this is a computed date, the tweet text was not read.

findings.claim: Medal is a closed-source Electron client plus a .NET recorder process. They talk over a local WebSocket JSON-RPC link, and the recorder is updated separately from the client.
findings.evidence: Third-party analysis of Medal-production-2637.461.1-Setup.exe found Electron 43.2.0 and a Velopack win-x64 package. The client hosts a WebSocket on 127.0.0.1 from port 10603; the recorder (MedalEncoder.exe) connects with '--electronPort <port> --environment <channel> --wsComms'. The recorder declares 34 JSON-RPC methods (StreamJsonRpc), and its AssetManager downloads checksummed recorder bundles and FFmpeg. The 2023 log shows 'Server running at http://127.0.0.1:10604/' and 'Available electron port not found, set port to default 10603'.

findings.claim: How Medal actually saves a clip is unknown: whether it cuts at keyframes with a stream copy or re-encodes, and what its keyframe interval is.
findings.evidence: scope.dll exposes scope_io_buffer_exportable_start_time/end_time, which suggests an exportable window aligned to keyframes (inference), but no GOP length or export method was found in any source.

design_recommendations: Keep Windows.Graphics.Capture as DuoClip's primary video source. It is what Medal ships as 'Advanced Window Capture' and needs no injection or admin rights. Plan for the limitations Medal documents: no exclusive fullscreen, a yellow border (removable only on Windows 11, via GraphicsCaptureAccess plus IsBorderRequired=false), and a cursor that is either invisible or set by IsCursorCaptureEnabled. Medal also claims recording continues while the game is minimized; test this on real machines.

Add a non-injection fallback for exclusive-fullscreen or WGC failures: DXGI Desktop Duplication of the game's monitor cropped to the window rect, which is what Medal's 2023 'standard window capture' appears to be. Pair it with WinEvent hooks for focus and move (SetWinEventHook works out of process, without injection). When the game is not in the foreground, show or record a placeholder and raise a UI warning, the way Medal shows 'Game out of Focus' with inactiveGame.png.

Do not build an injected game hook. Medal's hook is OBS graphics-hook-derived (GPLv2, shipped as a separate 'Host' component with a source offer). Medal documents conflicts with FACEIT AC and other overlays, a game crash has been blamed on it, and cheat makers reuse it. If you ever need FSE capture through a hook, isolate a GPL component as Medal does and get explicit anti-cheat vendor allowlisting first.

Implement post-roll the way Medal's Game API does (captureDelayMs and 'seconds before and after'). On a hotkey at global-clock time T, broadcast {clipId, T, N, M} to the peer. Each PC waits until its local mapping of T+M (plus a small safety margin) has been encoded, then exports [T−N, T+M] from its ring buffer. Start at the keyframe at or before T−N and record the exact trim offsets in the clip metadata, so the editor can trim precisely without re-encoding.

Size the RAM ring buffer from bitrate x (N + M + one GOP) x ~1.2 headroom. Medal's 120 s at 10 Mbps was 180 MB. Keep video and audio packet buffers separate, as scope.dll does. Offer a disk or mmap buffer option for long buffers or low-RAM PCs, and fall back to disk if RAM allocation fails. Medal recommends Disk if memory clips come out corrupt.

Timestamp every captured frame and audio packet with QPC at capture time (VFR, which is Medal's default FpsMode). Map those to the shared app clock, using the NTP-style offset over the WebRTC data channel, and never use wall-clock time. Store both the source QPC and the global-clock PTS in clip metadata so the two POVs can be aligned at frame level in the editor.

Audio: use WASAPI process loopback per process (game PID tree, plus Discord.exe on its own track), as Medal's 2026 defaults do (splitByProcess: game-audio, Discord.exe; MultipleAudioTracks=true). Microsoft documents a Windows 10 build 20348+ requirement, and Medal's 2023 logs show E_UNEXPECTED activation failures on Windows 10 19045. Detect failure and fall back to endpoint loopback with a visible warning. Many Brazilian users may still be on Windows 10 22H2.

Encoder: auto-select NVENC, AMF or QSV from a zero-copy NV12 path, default to H.264 for compatibility, offer HEVC/AV1 as opt-in, and keep a CPU fallback. Medal does the same. Consider raising GPU scheduling priority for the encoder device the way Medal does (SetGPUPriority, frame latency), but do not change system settings such as Windows Game Mode without the user's consent.

Temporary clip bucket: follow Medal's model of short-lived, signed, expiring URLs on a CDN (Akamai EdgeAuth-style exp/hmac tokens, GCS behind a CDN) and 14-day renewable private links. For DuoClip, use an object-storage bucket in São Paulo (e.g. GCS southamerica-east1, AWS sa-east-1, or Cloudflare R2), short-lived pre-signed PUT/GET URLs, and lifecycle-rule deletion (e.g. 24 h to 7 days). Use resumable or chunked ('progressive') uploads, and make the bucket a relay or fallback when the P2P transfer fails.

Default to uploading full-quality ranges after the clip is confirmed or after the match. Medal defaults to ON_GAME_EXIT and warns that instant uploads hurt in-game bandwidth. Send only the small 720p proxy immediately, and rate-limit uploads while a game is running.

Make the capture method a per-game setting fed by a remotely updatable game database, as Medal does with MedalGameInfo.db plus per-game ForceWindowCapture and AdvancedWindowCapture. That lets you push known-good modes (WGC vs DDA crop) for problem titles and OpenGL games, and recommend borderless windowed mode for FSE games.
open_questions: What technique does Medal's 'Experimental Capture' use? Is it a new scope.dll capture mode, a WGC variant, or something else? Not found.

Does current Medal (2026) still inject by default in anti-cheat-protected titles (Valorant/Vanguard, FACEIT CS2, EAC/BattlEye games), or does it fall back to window capture there? The marketing pages say 'no injection', but the binaries still ship the OBS hook. No game-by-game evidence was found.
Is medal-hook64.dll allowlisted by any anti-cheat vendor? No statements from Riot, FACEIT, Epic/EAC, BattlEye or Activision Ricochet were found.
Does Medal's Desktop/Screen Recording use DXGI Desktop Duplication or WGC monitor capture? Not confirmed.
Does Medal cut clips at keyframes with a stream copy or re-encode them, and what keyframe interval does it use? Not found.
Is cdn.medal.tv actually served by Akamai? This is inferred from the exp~data~hmac token format, and a 2026 job post lists both Cloudflare and Akamai at the edge.

Exact current wording of Medal support and learn pages could not be checked directly: medal.tv, support.medal.tv, medium.com and blog.medialooks.com were blocked by the egress proxy, so search-result excerpts were used. The Medal installer was not downloaded (medal.tv blocked with HTTP 403), so the bundled Licenses/obs_source_offer.txt was not read first-hand.
Is the 'Audio hook' seen in the 2023 logs a separate injected audio-capture mechanism, or just the process-loopback GAO stream? Unclear.

research.topic: Capture methods used by the main Windows game clipping/recording tools (NVIDIA, AMD, Xbox Game Bar, Steam, Discord, OBS, Medal, Overwolf/Outplayed/Insights, SteelSeries Moments, Eklipse, Allstar), and whether WGC window capture + hardware encoding is the most effective anti-cheat-safe approach for a new third-party app (DuoClip)
research.summary: The lowest-overhead capture paths belong to the GPU vendors. NVIDIA ShadowPlay / NVIDIA App Instant Replay uses NvFBC: ShadowPlay's own CaptureCore.log contains "NvFBCH264GrabFrame" errors, and NvFBC feeds NVENC on the same device. AMD's AMF SDK publicly ships a proprietary display-capture component that AMD says has lower latency and lower CPU/GPU cost than Desktop Duplication (DDA). Neither is a realistic default for DuoClip. NVIDIA has deprecated NvFBC on Windows 10+ (frozen at Capture SDK 7.1, last supported build 1803), recommends DDA or WGC instead, and treats NvFBC as licensed and not generally available on GeForce. Third parties only get it on GeForce by passing NVIDIA's own private key (a licensing problem), with an admin-only driver switch, and only one client can hold it at a time. AMD's API is monitor-level only. Xbox Game Bar/Game DVR offers no public API for recording other apps: Windows.Media.AppRecording only lets an app record its own content, and how Game Bar captures internally was not found. Steam Game Recording keeps a disk-backed background buffer (default 120 min, user-set disk budget) with a timeline where you choose a clip range after the fact. It only works where the Steam Overlay works, so it almost certainly relies on Valve's overlay hook (my inference; not documented). Discord's default capture injects a signed DLL (overlay technology). Discord offers WGC on Windows 10+ and says it will make WGC the default on Windows 11; Clips is built on Go Live streaming. OBS Game Capture is DLL injection: CreateRemoteThread+LoadLibraryW, or SetWindowsHookEx in its default "anti-cheat compatibility" mode, followed by Detours hooks on IDXGISwapChain::Present and a shared texture. It works under anti-cheat only because vendors trust OBS's specific signing certificate. Proof of that: the OBS 31 certificate change broke EAC games until each game updated its module, VAC/CS2 Trusted Mode allows no injection at all, and Vanguard broke OBS capture again in July 2026. Medal's default is a game hook; its "Advanced Window Capture" shows the Windows yellow border (i.e., WGC), and Medal recommends it for CS2, Rust and FiveM. Overwolf apps (Outplayed, Insights Capture) run an OBS-based engine whose main path is game capture via shared texture, with window capture as an option that is off by default. SteelSeries Moments' newer Windows 11 Capture Mode labels its game capture "Game Capture (WGC)". Eklipse and Allstar do not record locally at all: Eklipse processes Twitch VODs in the cloud, and Allstar renders clips in the cloud from match/demo data for CS2, Dota 2, LoL and Fortnite. No independent, controlled benchmark comparing hook vs WGC vs DDA game-FPS cost was found. The best hard numbers are one developer's single-machine test (rbuf): on a game running at 1,218 fps, the frame rate while recording was 1,164 with NvFBC, 1,158 with ShadowPlay and 1,071 with OBS display capture, and OBS also used 20.4% CPU in dwm.exe. That test also showed WGC CPU cost about equal to NvFBC's (1.93% vs 1.87%). OBS's own measurement put WGC at 200–800 µs per frame vs 300–500 µs for BitBlt. Verdict: driver capture is not legitimately available and hooks need per-anti-cheat whitelisting a new app will not have, so WGC window capture with zero-copy hardware encoding is the best available default. It is the same direction Discord, SteelSeries and Medal are moving. It needs a fallback for true exclusive-fullscreen games, where WGC returns the desktop: DDA monitor capture, or AMF display capture on AMD. Two WGC side effects should be measured with PresentMon: frames come at the DWM rate (possibly capped at 60 fps unless MinUpdateInterval is set), and on systems without MPO it can disable independent flip when VRR is on and a hardware cursor is shown. For CS2 and Dota 2, demo-based rendering (server-side GOTV demos, tick-accurate) is a real optional "perfect sync" multi-POV mode. It carries no voice audio and is not the players' literal screens.

findings.claim: NVIDIA deprecated NvFBC on Windows 10 and later and points developers to DDA and WGC instead.
findings.evidence: The NVIDIA tech bulletin and Capture SDK page (read via search snippets; direct fetch was blocked) say: "NVFBC is deprecated and will not receive any bug fixes or support for OS features on Windows 10 onwards. NVFBC capture functionality is frozen at Capture SDK 7.1" and "Last supported Windows 10 version is 1803, build 17134". The stated reason is that "Evolution of Windows 10 DDI is changing the fundamentals of GPU work scheduling. This makes NVFBC latency unpredictable." The bulletin names DDA (IDXGIOutputDuplication) and Windows.Graphics.Capture as the alternatives and links nvEncDXGIOutputDuplicationSample. The Sunshine docs (docs/configuration.md lines 2216-2252, commit 0594f62) mark nvfbc as "Applies to Linux only", and the vibeshine maintainer says "NVFBC is not supported anymore on windows."

findings.claim: NvFBC is not legitimately available to third-party apps on GeForce cards. The workarounds use NVIDIA's own private key or a DLL wrapper, need admin, and allow only one client at a time.
findings.evidence: A reply in the NVIDIA dev forum thread "If Steam can use nvFBC on GeForce why can I not develop my own program..." says NvFBC is a licensed product not supported on GeForce for all users. The rbuf README (lines 101-105) says "the driver only grants NvFBC sessions to callers that pass a private-data key. rbuf passes the key NVIDIA's own GeForce software uses". The same README says `--nvfbc-enable` must run "as administrator", sets NVFBCEnable, "takes effect after the display driver restarts", and that "while NVIDIA's own Instant Replay is running, its helper (nvsphelper64.exe) holds NvFBC". The nvidia-patch nvfbcwrp is a "Wrapper for NvFBC64.dll library which injects private keys into NvFBC_CreateEx calls" and works by replacing system DLLs.

findings.claim: NVIDIA ShadowPlay / NVIDIA App Instant Replay captures through NvFBC and encodes on NVENC. The NVIDIA App overlay also injects into games, and BattlEye has blocked NVIDIA's capture DLL.
findings.evidence: AlwaysShadow issue #20 (leumasme, 2024-07-07) quotes C:\ProgramData\NVIDIA Corporation\ShadowPlay\CaptureCore.log: "CVideoCapture::Capture: NvFBCH264GrabFrame failed with error = NVFBC_ERROR_PROTECTED_CONTENT". The rbuf README line 83 says ShadowPlay's log names `CFrameProviderFBCToDx9` (NvFBC to D3D9 NV12, then NVENC). The rbuf comparison table lists ShadowPlay as "Injects code into the game: yes (the NVIDIA App's overlay hook)" and says the overlay alone costs 1.3%. BattlEye logs show "[INFO] Blocked loading of file: C:\Windows\System32\nvspcap64.dll" (Destiny 2, 2021; R6 Extraction). A 2014 AnandTech review only inferred NvFBC use.

findings.claim: The only hard comparative numbers found: one developer's single-machine benchmark showing NvFBC ≈ ShadowPlay < OBS display capture in cost, and WGC CPU cost about equal to NvFBC.
findings.evidence: rbuf README lines 9-18. Setup: i9-14900KF, RTX 5070 Ti, Win11 23H2, 1080p NVENC H.264 16 Mbit/s, test game running at 1,218 fps. Game fps while recording: rbuf(NvFBC) 1,164, ShadowPlay 1,158, "OBS Studio (display capture)" 1,071. CPU at 60 fps: 1.95% / 2.58% / "9.9%, and 20.4% in dwm.exe". Memory: 104 / 724 / 241 MB. Line 99: an NvFBC session that was open but never grabbed from cost 34 of 1,219 fps (2.8%). Line 130: WGC path 1.93% CPU vs NvFBC 1.87%; NVENC busy 15% vs 17%. Caveats: author-run, one machine, and the extreme fps magnifies costs.

findings.claim: AMD exposes a public, driver-level (proprietary) display-capture API in its AMF SDK that AMD says beats DDA. It captures whole monitors only. Which capture path ReLive/Adrenalin itself uses is not documented.
findings.evidence: AMF repo amf/doc/AMF_Display_Capture_API.md lines 54-56 (commit 8c64800, 2026-09-29): "One legacy component is using the Microsoft DXGI Desktop Duplication API (DD), while the new component utilizes an AMD's proprietary API... it provides a more efficient way to perform display capture with lower latency and lower impact on the CPU and GPU performance." Init takes AMF_DISPLAYCAPTURE_MONITOR_INDEX. Frame rate 0 means capture at the "application's flip frequency (for full-screen applications) or by DWM". Output carries AMF_DISPLAYCAPTURE_FRAME_FLIP_TIMESTAMP. The AMD FAQ only says ReLive has "a minimal impact on performance" and that Instant Replay buffers up to 20 min. No source names ReLive's capture API (not found).

findings.claim: Xbox Game Bar / Game DVR cannot be driven by third-party apps to record other games. Its internal capture mechanism was not found.
findings.evidence: Microsoft Learn: AppRecordingManager "Enables a UWP app to save recordings and screenshots of its content", and CanRecord refers to the current app's own content. The GDK XAppCaptureStartUserRecord is for the game itself, and its page says Windows support "will be added in a future release". Windows 10-era coverage says background recording was off by default because of performance on all but high-end GPUs, and that Game Bar records one app at a time and cannot record Explorer or the desktop. No Microsoft document says whether bcastdvr.exe uses WGC, DWM or something else.

findings.claim: Steam Game Recording keeps a disk-backed background buffer with a timeline and markers, and lets you pick any clip range after the fact. It depends on the Steam Overlay; the capture mechanism itself is undocumented (likely Valve's overlay hook).
findings.evidence: Steam Support (via search): two modes, "Record in background" and on demand. You set the maximum disk space, and "once that space on your hard drive is full, the recordings will be overwritten". Default is the last 120 minutes. The Clip button "will drop a clip suggestion on the timeline that you can adjust by dragging the end points". Markers come from achievements, screenshots, the game Timeline API (ISteamTimeline AddInstantaneousTimelineEvent, where "Negative times indicate an event that happened in the past") and Ctrl+F12. It uses AMD/NVIDIA hardware encoding by default. It works with games compatible with the Steam Overlay and "only records the game window". Clips are stored in a Steam timeline format and exported to MP4. Remote Play logs show a "Game polled D3D11 NV12 + NVENC" capture path. Mechanism = inferred.

findings.claim: Discord's default capture is an injected signed DLL (overlay technology), with WGC as the alternative it plans to make default on Windows 11. Clips builds on Go Live streaming.
findings.evidence: Discord support article 9410427556375: "Our current default capture method uses similar technology to capture your screen that is used for overlay, and our signed DLL is injected into the application to extract rendered frames". Also: "Windows Graphics Capture is available on Windows 10 and above", "On Windows 11 and higher, we will change the default capture method to Windows Graphics Capture", WGC "does not work for full screen exclusive (FSE) games", Discord falls back when it detects FSE, and it recommends Borderless. The Clips article: Early Access for Nitro, "there are two ways to create Clips while you're streaming", 30 s / 1 min / 2 min, Alt+C, and it "may impact your game performance if you have lower end hardware".

findings.claim: OBS Game Capture is DLL injection followed by in-process Present hooks that share frames via a shared texture. The default mode uses SetWindowsHookEx; the direct mode uses CreateRemoteThread.
findings.evidence: obs-studio commit c5bcbca (2026-10-05). shared/obs-inject-library/inject-library.c lines 44/49/54: VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, then CreateRemoteThread(LoadLibraryW). Line 117: set_windows_hook_ex(WH_GETMESSAGE,...). plugins/win-capture/game-capture.c line 2117 sets SETTING_ANTI_CHEAT_HOOK default true; line 952 logs "using helper (%s hook)" with "compatibility" or "direct". plugins/win-capture/graphics-hook/dxgi-capture.cpp lines 325-342 DetourAttach RealPresent/RealPresent1 ("Hooked IDXGISwapChain::Present"). game-capture.c lines 1597-1671 handle the shared texture ("shared texture capture successful"), with a shmem fallback.

findings.claim: Hook-based capture works under anti-cheat only through per-vendor, per-certificate whitelisting. A new app would not have that whitelisting, and CS2/VAC allows no injection at all in Trusted Mode.
findings.evidence: OBS KB "Capture Hook Certificate Update" (via search): OBS 31.0 ships the hook "only with the new certificate". EAC: "An updated EAC module is available, but requires game developers to manually switch to the new version". VAC: "Valve does not allow any injection unless the game is running in 'Untrusted' mode via the -allow_third_party_software launch parameter". Vanguard: update planned (table dated 2024-08-21). Valve's Steam FAQ: Trusted Mode "blocks third-party files from interacting with the game and is enabled by default", because injection "is used by common applications as well as cheats". In July 2026 Vanguard broke OBS Game Capture until Riot patched it.

findings.claim: OBS's own non-hook capture logic: Window Capture's Automatic mode uses BitBlt except for listed window classes (which get WGC); Display Capture's Automatic mode uses DXGI except on multi-GPU laptops or monitors DXGI can't see (which get WGC). OBS disables the WGC border.
findings.evidence: plugins/win-capture/window-capture.c lines 113-168: wgc_partial_match_classes {Chrome, Mozilla} and whole-match classes (UWP, Office, SDL_app, Roblox "WINDOWSCLIENT"...); otherwise METHOD_BITBLT. plugins/win-capture/duplicator-monitor-capture.c lines 250-277: METHOD_DXGI unless dxgi_index == -1, or on a battery-capable system with ≥2 adapters, then METHOD_WGC. libobs-winrt/winrt-capture.cpp line 251 CreateForWindow; line 320 session.IsBorderRequired(false). OBS admin R1CH: "The main benefit of WGC capture is that it works cross-GPU with no user intervention. DXGI requires OBS to run on the same GPU as the display."

findings.claim: OBS's WGC measurement: WGC costs about the same as BitBlt on the capture side (slightly more CPU with more variance, slightly less GPU).
findings.evidence: OBS PR #2208 "Windows Graphics Capture support" (jpark37, merged 2020-02-23): WGC measured "a bit more expensive than BitBlt", about 200–800 µs vs 300–500 µs, with GPU use looking slightly lower for WGC in Task Manager (noisy). Known drawbacks listed: the yellow border and an always-captured cursor.

findings.claim: Medal: the default recorder uses a game hook. "Advanced Window Capture" is WGC-based (shown by the Windows yellow border), and Medal recommends it for CS2, Rust and FiveM. There is also a monitor 'Desktop Capture'. Medal does not publicly name its APIs or say whether it is OBS-based.
findings.evidence: Medal black-screen article: "Some overlays and recorders may interfere with Medal's hook"; it also mentions DXGI capture. A Medal job post: "hooking into engines... DirectX, Vulkan, OpenGL". Advanced Window Capture article: captures "even when your game window is minimized"; "The yellow box is a Windows security feature indicating that your game window is being recorded by Medal only when Advanced Window Capture is in use"; "will not work if your game is in exclusive fullscreen mode"; helpful "for games like Rust, FiveM, and CS2". Medal also documents the Windows 11 "Let apps turn off the screenshot border" setting. The WGC mapping is my inference from the border, which Microsoft documents as part of WGC. No source says whether Medal uses libobs (not found).

findings.claim: Overwolf apps (Outplayed, and Insights Capture, which uses Overwolf's engine) record with an OBS-based engine. Its main path is game capture via shared texture; window capture is optional and off by default.
findings.evidence: Overwolf dev docs: the OBS log is ow_obs_*.log and lists a source named "OW Game capture"; support says "Overwolf's recording system is based on OBS". @overwolf/types 3.51.0 overwolf.d.ts: "Do not start video replay service in case shared texture is not supported" (disable_when_sht_not_supported); interface GameWindowCapture { enable_when_available: boolean; //Disabled by default } (lines 4159-4162); keep_game_capture_on_lost_focus; is_game_window_capture event flag (line 837); encoders NVENC/AMF/QSV/x264. Insights.gg says it uses "the core OBS recording tech provided by Overwolf". Overwolf support: FACEIT AC "may block Overwolf from using game events" in CS2.

findings.claim: SteelSeries Moments moved from a hook-first Auto mode to a Windows 11 'Capture Mode' that labels its game capture 'Game Capture (WGC)', with screen capture as the fallback.
findings.evidence: Older article: Game Capture "directly 'hooks' into the game... offers slightly better performance than screen capture, and may be blocked by certain games"; Auto tries the hook and falls back to screen capture. Newer "What is Moments Capture Mode" / "How to Enable" articles: two modes, "Game Capture (WGC)" and Screen Capture; Windows 11 only ("Earlier versions will default to Screen Capture only"); beta toggle. FACEIT/ESEA article warns that Auto in Valve matchmaking "could theoretically lower your trust factor". Encoding is described as running on the GPU's dedicated encoder.

findings.claim: Eklipse does not capture locally. It clips Twitch VODs on its servers after the stream ends.
findings.evidence: Eklipse pages: connect Twitch and enable VOD access; "processing runs on Eklipse's cloud servers, with zero FPS impact on your PC"; it cannot clip games that were never broadcast. These are vendor pages.

findings.claim: Allstar renders clips server-side from match/demo data with no screen recording, for CS2, Dota 2, League of Legends and Fortnite. It offers a partner API and help-center flows for Gamers Club (a Brazilian CS platform) and squad montages.
findings.evidence: allstar.gg/howitworks: "No screen recording or live streaming required"; "Never drop FPS again – Allstar makes your clips for you, all using the cloud". CS2 FAQ: clips take "about 30 minutes"; partner delivery via Leetify, FACEIT and Refrag. QuickFrag: "powered by the Allstar partner API... Allstar processes your demo in the cloud". Help-center titles found in search: "Claim Clips - Gamers Club" and "Match/Squad Montage - FAQ". Status page, July 2026: a CS2 update broke clip generation for demos from older versions, later restored.

findings.claim: Demo-based rendering gives tick-accurate multi-POV sync for CS2, because one server-side GOTV demo contains every player. It does not reproduce the players' literal screens, their Discord voice, or footage from games without demos.
findings.evidence: CS2 demo guides: GOTV demos are server-side and record positions, shots and events per tick (CS2 = 64 ticks/s), and "can be slightly smoothed compared to what players actually saw". POV demos are client-side and single-viewpoint. Rendering means playing the demo in the game client and capturing it (startmovie/HLAE style). Allstar takes about 30 min per clip, and game updates broke older demos (July 2026). That rendering N POVs over the same tick range yields perfect sync is my inference.

findings.claim: WGC cannot capture true exclusive-fullscreen (Legacy Flip) games and shows the desktop instead. DDA can capture fullscreen DirectX apps but must be recreated across mode switches.
findings.evidence: Discord: WGC "does not work for full screen exclusive (FSE) games". Medal: Advanced Window Capture fails in exclusive fullscreen. rbuf README line 142: an exclusive-fullscreen test game showed "PresentMon shows Legacy Flip", NvFBC captured it, and "Windows Graphics Capture's is the desktop". Microsoft (DDA driver doc): "even full screen DirectX applications can be duplicated", but ReleaseFrame docs say mode changes or switching to a full-screen app invalidate the duplicator (DXGI_ERROR_ACCESS_LOST, so it must be recreated). DuplicateOutput1 takes supported formats for fullscreen surfaces.

findings.claim: WGC tuning knobs: the frame rate may be capped at 60 fps unless MinUpdateInterval is set (newer Windows builds), and removing the border needs feature detection plus user consent or a Windows 11 setting.
findings.evidence: Sunshine src/platform/windows/display_wgc.cpp lines 150-165 (commit 0594f62): it sets IsBorderRequired(false) when present and MinUpdateInterval(4ms) // 250Hz, otherwise warns "Screen capture may be capped to 60fps on this device for this release of Windows". Win32CaptureSample issue #82 ties MinUpdateInterval to the 26100 APIs (24H2; version not officially confirmed). Microsoft Learn: IsBorderRequired is honored only after RequestAccessAsync(Borderless) consent (graphicsCaptureWithoutBorder capability), and a denial is silently ignored. Medal points users to the Windows 11 "Let apps turn off the screenshot border" setting.

findings.claim: WGC frames carry QPC timestamps, the same clock WASAPI uses, so audio and video line up without clock translation. That helps the app-level global clock design.
findings.evidence: Sunshine display_wgc.cpp line 232: `out_time = consumed_frame.SystemRelativeTime().count(); // raw ticks from query performance counter`. rbuf README line 119: "Every timestamp is the performance counter in 100 ns units, the clock Windows Graphics Capture and WASAPI already use, so tracks line up without translation". rbuf measured A/V offset of about 18 ms on window capture (including Windows audio output latency) and 35 ms on WGC screen capture.

findings.claim: WGC side effects that can cost the player latency or smoothness: it can disable independent flip (without MPO, when VRR is on and a hardware cursor is shown), switches Windows to a software cursor, delivers frames at the DWM rate, and there are anecdotal stutter reports.
findings.evidence: Lossless Scaling 24H2 note: "without MPO support... in games where a hardware cursor is displayed and VRR is enabled, WGC disables independent flip mode globally", and WGC "captures game frames at DWM framerate regardless of game framerate". The same note says Microsoft fixed a five-year-old WGC bug in 24H2, while DXGI DDA became "heavily reliant on MPO". CaptureEngine README: a WGC session can make Windows use a software-rendered cursor. A Steam CS2 thread reports the OBS 'Windows 10' (WGC) method was "a stuttery mess" for one user (anecdotal). No controlled PresentMon study of WGC's effect on game presentation mode was found.

findings.claim: Anti-cheat stance of non-injected capture (WGC/DDA): nothing touches the game process, and it is the configuration recommended for anti-cheat games. A game can still opt out via display affinity, and window capture can't see higher-privilege windows.
findings.evidence: CaptureEngine README: "Any feature that depends on CaptureEngine's injected hook DLL should be treated as unsafe with anti-cheat software", and WGC/DXGI with dll_injection=never is "the likely-compatible configuration, not a universal guarantee". OBS community advice for CS2 Trusted Mode: use windowed/borderless plus Window Capture. Microsoft: SetWindowDisplayAffinity(WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE) (Win10 2004+) removes the game's own window from capture; it is not DRM. One GGPoker forum anecdote suggests a client reacted to WGC-based tools. No anti-cheat vendor documentation on WGC was found.

findings.claim: No independent, controlled benchmark compares hook vs WGC vs DDA game-FPS impact. The precise percentages that circulate are unreliable.
findings.evidence: Searches of the OBS forums, GitHub (Sunshine, Magpie, CaptureEngine) and benchmark sites found no such test. obs-versions.com publishes two contradictory tables (3/5/7% vs 5/8/12% GPU for Game/Window/Display) with no method. The OBS Classic help file calls window capture "almost as good as game capture", and on Windows 8+ monitor capture "highly efficient". Magpie recommends Graphics Capture for "the best compatibility and smoothness" without numbers. An old D3DShot benchmark put GDI/BitBlt at about 30% of DDA's frame rate.

findings.claim: Hardware encoding is the main reason modern recorders cost little FPS. Every major tool uses NVENC/AMF/QSV. Older ShadowPlay tests show small but nonzero cost.
findings.evidence: Valve: Game Recording uses AMD/NVIDIA video encoders, and "non-AMD and -NVIDIA GPUs may see significant performance impacts". SteelSeries: Moments "uses a section of your graphics card dedicated to encoding video". Techtesters measured ShadowPlay at about 3% with no frametime/1%-low penalty. PCWorld saw a budget rig drop from about 56 to 44 fps while recording. NVIDIA App (2024) added 120 fps AV1 with "minimal impact" (no number).

findings.claim: GeForce NVENC concurrent-session limit is 8 per system, shared with everything else encoding on the PC. This matters if DuoClip runs a ring-buffer encode plus a live 720p proxy encode alongside Discord or ShadowPlay.
findings.evidence: An NVIDIA dev forum thread quoting the Video Codec SDK 12.2 application note gives 8 sessions for non-qualified (GeForce) GPUs, requiring Windows driver ≥551.76. Earlier limits were 2, then 3, then 5. One user still observed only 3 on driver 530.

findings.claim: Efficiency ranking (lowest to highest game cost): (1) driver framebuffer capture (NvFBC→NVENC on one device; AMD AMF display capture); (2) in-process Present hook + shared texture; (3) WGC window; (4) WGC monitor / DDA whole display (DDA showed the heaviest DWM CPU load in the one benchmark); (5) GDI BitBlt. Only 3–5, plus AMF capture on AMD, are both legitimately available to and anti-cheat-safe for a new third-party app.
